questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To find a good university, nice city, nice nature for hikes

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. Nice to go to an English speaking country, and I quickly met a lot of exchange students so we could help each other out. UoE is very aware of their students' well-being.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: UoE has a Visiting Student Advisor who reaches out to you individually and you have to attend a zoom meeting where you are informed. All introduction activities can be found on an app.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Most introduction activities were targeted freshers, so I did not find it necessary to stress about attending them

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of different student accommodation at different price ranges. However, you're only guaranteed if you stay for a full year or come from outside Europe. I applied for the cheapest available (around £400/month) and got nothing until I called and begged and got one of the remaining rooms (around £800+/month)

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I lived in catered accommodation, meaning breakfast and dinner was a buffet in a dining hall. I had access to a pantry room with a microwave, a toaster, and a kettle.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
It is hard to get! Apply in good time and call them if you don't hear from them! I only know people who got a room because they called several times. It is also quite expensive - I payed 29.000 DKK for four months. I would try to find housing on my own, but there is a lot of scamming and most rentals demand a UK guarantor.

Living in a catered accommodation is nice, because you get to eat with your friends on campus every morning and evening. The food is alright but the dining hall is very loud (housing up to 2000 students). But I personally prefer cooking on my own, so I missed that a lot!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I thought it was a confusing process but KU gave me the names of Danish exchange students and we helped each other to figure it out

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to meet up at an office at Old College and get our arrival registrated by showing passport and flight tickets. we also had to meet up at another office and get registrated. we got the information on mail and booked time for both.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Visiting Student Advisor! You can always write to him/her and you get a personal advisor. I didn't really use it, but I know many people did successfully.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very! I didn't get everything I applied for, but ended up with something I enjoyed even more.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read (and organize) your mails - you'll get a lot!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Lectures were similar to KU, tutorials were an easier level. I've been told that it's very easy to pass your exams when they're essays, but I haven't had feedback yet, so I don't know about that

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar! Lectures were the same. Tutorials were smaller groups.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Culture and Power
Anthropology of Health and Healing
War and Peace: Anthropological Perspectives

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them, but especially Culture and Power!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I joined The Hillwalking Club, were we went on weekend trips. Each trip was £50 and really worth it!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Accommodation was so much more expensive than expected!
Transportation! I walked everywhere. Only if I took the bus outside the city and it was still quite cheap. I did although go on roadtrips and likewise which isn't calculated above, but that was also an acceptable price.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sooo many clubs and societies! I had nice friend groups so I didn't engage in much of it, but I really recommend Hillwalking Club! The tickets are very popular, so be quick for the trips, but I got all the trips I wanted, so it's not impossible.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Clubs and societies. Lots and lots and well informed at your arrival

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hillwalking Club!! Perfect and easy way to experience the incredible nature!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Other than the club I went on several weekend trips. Go on a roadtrip (we went for 5 days), go t oGlasgow (maybe for a concert) or other cities. A small country with a lot to offer!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy! Many international students and very European milleau.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: People are very outgoing, so literally just reach out and you will be rewarded :)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The pedestrian crossing turns green both ways at the same time. More seriously, people are pretty young when starting university there, so most of my neighbors were 18 years

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their love for dogs and cozy cafes - and how you often find both the same place

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Go hiking / see nature
- Call student accommodation early if you apply there
- Bring room for lots of nice 2nd hand shopping

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Shout out to university fitness center. They put their logo on everything, including weight plates. I payed £100 for one semester of fitness AND bouldering/roped climbing. Very nice climbing staff.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting nice people and going nice places

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding time for everything. It's a big plus that the semester is quite short cause I needed a lot of time to relax after coming home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Look up the location of your classes. I had 10 minutes between two classes and a 14 minute walk - but I managed, so not your biggest worries.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
